name: IN-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+16 partisan lean in a heavily Republican district
Incumbent Stutzman running with a large fundraising edge
Prediction markets price Democratic chances near 5%
model.rationale: The district's R+16 lean, Stutzman's incumbency and 6-to-1 fundraising advantage, and markets pricing Democrats around 5% all point to a safe Republican hold; no polls or expert ratings suggest any reason to move toward the challenger.
model.watch: A scandal or unexpected incumbent retirement would be the main route to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Indiana's 3rd district is a deeply Republican seat, with a partisan lean of about 16 points toward the GOP. Republican incumbent Marlin Stutzman is running for reelection after winning renomination, and he holds a large financial advantage, having raised roughly $840,000 to Democrat Kelly Thompson's $136,000, with Thompson left with only about $6,000 on hand. Outside spending has been modest and one-sided, favoring Republicans.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and money. Prediction markets give Democrats only about a 5% chance of winning. The expected Republican margin is roughly 17 points, and the seat is rated Safe R.
